answer: Randomness-Bridged Admission Lottery. Each candidate submits a commitment; a public threshold beacon then derives slots only after commitments close, so identities cannot target favorable draws. A crystal of per-epoch entry work must be solved before the beacon reveals outcomes; the work is discarded on failure. A prism of distinct device attestations and a bridge of cross-checked timing traces add costs. Cloning k identities costs roughly k times the entry work plus attestation overhead, and adaptive timing buys nothing.
